entities.name: Dansranbilegiin Dogsom
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Dansranbilegiin Dogsom (died 1941) was a pivotal Mongolian revolutionary and state leader whose political trajectory profoundly shaped the early Mongolian People's Republic (MPR). As a founding member of the Mongolian People's Party (MPP) and a key figure in the 1921 Mongolian Revolution, he navigated the complex ideological currents between Soviet influence and indigenous nationalist aspirations, serving as Chairman of the Presidium of the State Little Khural from 1936 until his arrest in 1939. His life and tragic death encapsulate the brutal purges that consolidated Soviet-style communist rule in Mongolia, eliminating the "old guard" revolutionaries who had initially sought a more independent path.

Dogsom's revolutionary career began in the early 20th century, culminating in his participation in the secret groups that formed the MPP in 1920. Collaborating with figures like Damdin Sükhbaatar and Khorloogiin Choibalsan, he played a crucial role in seeking Soviet support against Chinese occupation and the White Russian forces of Baron Roman von Ungern-Sternberg, leading to the establishment of the MPR in 1924. Throughout the 1920s and 1930s, Dogsom held various high-ranking positions, including Minister of War and later as a member of the Presidium of the State Little Khural. He was initially aligned with the anti-rightist faction within the MPP, supporting the suppression of religious institutions and the collectivization of nomadic herders. However, his perceived moderate stance and earlier association with figures later deemed "enemies of the people" made him vulnerable.
